headline: AWS growth accelerated to 39% in Q3 FY2026, but trailing free cash flow turned to a $42.4bn outflow as AI capex rose.
summary: Through Q3 FY2026 (ended September 30, 2026), operating income was $23.9bn, $27.5bn and $28.1bn in Q1, Q2 and Q3, against $18.4bn, $19.2bn and $17.4bn a year earlier [1]. AWS sales grew 28%, 37% and 39%, and AWS operating income rose to $14.2bn, $16.6bn and $17.8bn [1]. Reported net income is not a clean guide: Anthropic-related gains were $16.8bn pre-tax in Q1, and Q2 included $53.4bn of non-operating other income, mainly from Anthropic [1]. Cash flow weakened. Trailing free cash flow moved from a $1.2bn inflow at Q1 to a $42.4bn outflow at Q3, as cash capex reached $75.9bn in Q3 against $34.2bn a year earlier [1][2]. Total debt was $271.9bn at September 30, against $153.0bn at year-end, and net cash was -$157.7bn [2][3]. AWS compounding (T1) strengthened and the valuation exposure (T3) is intact. The free-cash-flow recovery (T2) is weakened. Legal costs (T4) show no new reserves in the filings reviewed [2][4]. Consensus FY2026 EPS is $12.80, a 19.9x forward P/E [3].
results_commentary:
Q1 FY2026 net sales rose 17% to $181.5bn (15% excluding FX), and operating income rose to $23.9bn from $18.4bn [1]. AWS drove the quarter: sales rose 28% to $37.6bn and operating income rose to $14.2bn from $11.5bn [1]. Net income of $30.3bn ($2.78 per diluted share) included $16.8bn of pre-tax Anthropic gains, so the EPS beat against a $1.65 estimate reflects investment marks rather than operations [1][3]. Q2 FY2026 net sales rose 20% to $200.6bn, and operating income rose to $27.5bn from $19.2bn [1]. AWS sales grew 37% to $42.2bn, the fastest growth in 18 quarters, and AWS operating income rose to $16.6bn from $10.2bn [1]. Part of the Q2 retail growth reflects Prime Day moving into June for most large countries [1]. Q2 EPS of $5.75 included $53.4bn of non-operating income, mainly from Anthropic [1][3]. Cash flow began to deteriorate: Q2 cash capex was $53.1bn against $31.4bn a year earlier [2].

Q3 FY2026 is where profit and cash flow diverged. Net sales rose 12% to $201.9bn, and management said the Prime Day shift cut about 400 basis points from Q3 growth, so the underlying rate was nearer 16% (illustrative) [1]. North America slowed to 6% and International to 5%, or 8% excluding FX [1]. Operating income still rose to $28.1bn from $17.4bn, and the 13.9% operating margin was described as Amazon's highest ever [1]. AWS sales grew 39% to $46.0bn, and AWS operating income rose to $17.8bn from $11.4bn [1]. Diluted EPS fell to $1.89 from $1.95, because the year-ago quarter included $9.5bn of Anthropic gains; EPS missed the $1.96 estimate by 3.5% [1][3]. Operating profit grew while reported EPS fell, so the reported earnings line depends on the timing of investment marks.

Cash flow is the weakest line. Trailing free cash flow fell from a $1.2bn inflow at Q1 to a $7.6bn outflow at Q2 and a $42.4bn outflow at Q3, driven by $94.8bn more net property and equipment purchases than a year earlier [1]. Nine-month cash capex was $172.2bn against $89.9bn [2]. Management expects cash capex to "meaningfully increase in 2027" [2]. Operating cash flow was positive at $113.8bn for nine months, but financing inflows of $111.8bn covered the gap, and total debt rose to $271.9bn [2][3]. Two equity investments added to the cash need: $50.0bn in OpenAI Series C preferred stock over nine months and $10.0bn in Anthropic nonvoting preferred stock [2]. Note on data: the multi-quarter scorecard labels its "Q2 FY2026" column as ending 2026-09-30, and those figures match the Q3 release. I used the release dates and did not use the scorecard's Q2 column.

thesis_check.thesis: T1: AWS keeps compounding fast enough to fund the capex build-out.
thesis_check.signpost: AWS sales growth of at least 18% and operating margin of at least 35% in each 2026 quarterly report (invalidation: growth below 15% or margin below 33%).
thesis_check.evidence: AWS sales grew 28%, 37% and 39% in Q1, Q2 and Q3 FY2026 [1]. AWS operating margin, derived from segment sales and operating income, was above the 35% signpost in each quarter (illustrative calculation from [1]). AWS operating income rose to $17.8bn in Q3 from $11.4bn a year earlier [1].

thesis_check.thesis: T2: Capex peaks and free cash flow recovers in 2026.
thesis_check.signpost: FY2026 free cash flow above $25 billion in the February 2027 10-K, with capex growth slowing (invalidation: FY2026 free cash flow at or below $11.2 billion, or new borrowing used to fund operations).
thesis_check.evidence: Trailing free cash flow moved from a $1.2bn inflow at Q1 to a $7.6bn outflow at Q2 and a $42.4bn outflow at Q3 [1]. Nine-month cash capex rose to $172.2bn from $89.9bn, and management expects capex to increase further in 2027 [2]. Nine-month operating cash flow of $113.8bn was positive, but financing inflows of $111.8bn funded the gap [2]. Trailing free cash flow is far below the signpost path, so the FY2026 test is at risk; the 10-K will confirm.

thesis_check.thesis: T3: The valuation requires above-trend growth, so returns are exposed to any slowdown.
thesis_check.signpost: FY2026 reported revenue at or above the $829 billion consensus in the February 2027 10-K (invalidation: FY2026 revenue growth below 15%).
thesis_check.evidence: Consensus FY2026 revenue is $829.2bn, +15.7% [3]. Quarterly net sales were $181.5bn, $200.6bn and $201.9bn, with Q3 growth of 12% held down by the Prime Day shift [1]. The reverse DCF implies 19.3% revenue growth against 15.7% consensus, and an implied IRR of 8.3% against a 12.4% WACC [3].

thesis_check.thesis: T4: Regulatory and legal costs stay contained relative to the earnings base.
thesis_check.signpost: No new settlement or tax reserve above $2.5 billion disclosed in 2026 filings (invalidation: a new material FTC settlement or an adverse ruling in the Indian cloud-services tax case).
thesis_check.evidence: The releases and 10-Q MD&A excerpts reviewed disclose no new FTC settlement or tax reserve above $2.5bn [1][2]. The legal proceedings and tax notes were not in the excerpts provided, so this status rests on the MD&A review and should be checked against those notes. The $1bn Built Together and $1.5bn wage programmes announced in Q3 are operating commitments, not legal reserves [1].

risk_update: Materialised: the capital intensity risk. Trailing free cash flow is a $42.4bn outflow, and total debt rose to $271.9bn from $153.0bn at year-end, a $119bn increase [1][2][3]. The filings describe the borrowing as funding investment, not operations. New: the investment risk now sits in two AI counterparties. Amazon has committed $50.0bn to OpenAI preferred stock and $10.0bn to Anthropic preferred stock, and Anthropic gains drive reported EPS in Q1 and Q2 [1][2]. The Q3 release lists memory-chip supply as a risk to demand and costs, and the 10-Q risk factors on competition are unchanged [1][2]. Eased: none of the risks reviewed eased. The FTC and Indian tax matters were not updated in the excerpts provided.
outlook: The Q3 release's guidance section was cut off in the data, so no Q4 guidance figures are reported here. Consensus FY2026 revenue is $829.2bn (+15.7%) and EPS $12.80, the latter 0.2% lower than 90 days earlier [3]. FY2027 consensus is revenue of $960.5bn (+15.8%) and EPS of $10.67, up 1.5% over 90 days [3]. Management projects AWS growth above 40% in 2027 and 2028; this is a management projection, not guidance [1]. Watch Q4 AWS growth against 39%, the Q4 revenue needed for consensus, and whether Anthropic marks keep moving EPS. For T2, the test is the FY2026 free cash flow figure in the February 2027 10-K.
